blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Feed-forward geometry models such as VGGT recover camera parameters, depth maps, and point maps from one to hundreds of views in a single forward pass, making them powerful backbones for multi-view 3D perception. However, VGGT's global attention is quadratic in the number of frames and dominates end-to-end runtime on long sequences, which has motivated a range of training-free efficiency methods such as token merging. These methods, however, come with a drop in accuracy that makes them hard to use in place of VGGT. We propose GPA-VGGT, a training-free acceleration method that replaces global attention in early blocks with frame attention augmented by a shared cross-frame K/V set. In the remaining blocks, we merge only keys and values while preserving all queries, restore the attention mass of the tokens each merged key represents, and randomly project the matching metric to 128 dimensions to reduce matching cost. Across diverse multi-view geometry tasks, GPA-VGGT provides training-free acceleration at speedups comparable to prior work while preserving the information required for precise geometric estimation, retaining over 99% of VGGT's pose accuracy under AUC@3.

blocks.en: 2.1 VGGT Acceleration
blocks.zh: 2.1 VGGT加速

blocks.en:
VGGT [ 1 ] is a feed-forward multi-view geometry model that takes a set of unposed images as
input and jointly predicts camera parameters, depth maps, point maps, and tracking
features for all views. Each view is tokenized by a DINOv2 [ 24 ] encoder,
and its Transformer [ 25 ] alternates between frame attention and
global attention. Although global attention is essential for establishing multi-view
consistency, its quadratic complexity with respect to the number of tokens makes it the
primary computational bottleneck for long image sequences.

blocks.en:
FastVGGT [ 2 ] was the first method to introduce token merging into VGGT. To
address token collapse in long sequences, it uses a partitioning strategy tailored to the
multi-frame layout and preserves a subset of salient tokens from merging.
FasterVGGT [ 6 ] replaces dense global attention with training-free
block-sparse attention, retaining selected block interactions based on coarse attention
patterns and geometrically meaningful correspondences. AVGGT [ 3 ] replaces early
global blocks with frame attention and applies uniform grid-based subsampling to
patch tokens in the remaining global blocks. Its design is motivated by the observation
that global attention supports cross-view alignment through sparse spatial
correspondences rather than dense token-to-token interactions.
HTTM [ 10 ] performs head-wise temporal token merging with temporal reordering
to preserve feature diversity after head concatenation.
Although these methods
provide substantial acceleration, their accuracy degradation becomes more apparent under
strict metrics such as AUC@3, which are sensitive to fine-grained camera-pose errors. Our
method instead preserves the information required for precise geometric estimation and pose accuracy at AUC@3.

blocks.en: 2.2 Token Merging
blocks.zh: 2.2 合并

blocks.en:
ToMe [ 15 ] was first introduced as a training-free approach to improve the
throughput of vision transformers, and was later extended to diffusion, video, and language models.
ToMe partitions tokens in each block into source and destination sets and merges tokens
based on the similarity of their attention keys. Since a merged key represents multiple
tokens, ToMe adds the logarithm of the group size to the attention logit so that the
merged key receives their combined attention mass. ToMeSD [ 16 ] adapts this procedure to Stable Diffusion by
selecting destination tokens from a fixed 2D grid and computing similarity from the
block input rather than attention keys. It also omits this correction and
uses a merge–unmerge scheme to preserve dense outputs. FastVGGT adopts this
ToMeSD-style token merging for a 3D geometry backbone, where such design choices can
lead to fine-grained information loss and accuracy degradation in precise geometry
estimation.

blocks.en:
The aggregator is not uniformly tolerant to merging: blocks 13 13 – 16 16 are substantially
more sensitive than the remaining merged blocks, and errors introduced in this range are
amplified rather than corrected by subsequent blocks. This sensitivity follows from the
attention patterns. In the middle blocks, queries attend sharply to a small number of
keys, particularly cross-view correspondences; averaging keys can therefore dilute the
information carried by the most relevant key. In later blocks, attention is more diffuse
and primarily directed toward global sink tokens, making merging less disruptive. We
consequently use a merge ratio of 0.2 0.2 for blocks 13 13 – 16 16 and retain the ratio of 0.9 0.9 for all other blocks in the merging window.

The similarity scores are used only to select destination indices and are discarded

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We identify three sources of accuracy degradation in accelerated VGGT:
information loss from query merging, incorrect attention mass after K/V
merging, and the removal of early cross-frame context. GPA-VGGT addresses these
issues through Query-Preserving K/V Merging with + log ⁡ s +\log s correction, Pooled
Cross-Frame Broadcast, and low-dimensional matching.
Across diverse multi-view geometry evaluations, GPA-VGGT reduces
inference time while preserving vanilla VGGT’s accuracy under both standard
and strict metrics.

blocks.en: Appendix A Custom Triton Kernels
blocks.zh: 附录 A 自定义三角内核

blocks.en: A.1 Attention with a Per-Key Additive Bias
blocks.zh: A.1 注意Per-Key Additive Bias

blocks.en:
The standard attention interface treats the + log ⁡ s +\log s correction as a mask and therefore
falls back to a slower implementation. For a 200 200 -frame sequence, this fallback takes 2,142 2{,}142 ms, compared with 948 948 ms for unbiased fused attention—more time than key
merging saves in the merged global-attention block.
blocks.zh:
标准关注界面将+log QQs QQlog 校正作为遮罩处理,因此
执行速度又放慢。 对于200200帧的序列来说,这个倒置需要2,142 2{,}142毫秒,而948,948毫秒用于无偏见的引信注意——比钥匙需要更多的时间.
合并在合并的全局关注区块中的保存 。

blocks.en:
Because the correction depends only on the key index, our Triton kernel adds it directly
to each score tile inside the online-softmax loop, preserving the streaming structure of
FlashAttention [ 21 ] . We avoid masked loads by clamping out-of-range key
indices and assigning duplicate columns a − 10 9 -10^{9} bias. This avoids padding and copying
K/V tensors; only the small bias vector is padded. The bias is also pre-scaled on the
host, avoiding conversion within the inner loop. For a 200 200 -frame sequence, our
kernel takes 984 984 ms: only 4 % 4\% slower than unbiased fused attention and 2.18 × 2.18\times faster than the fallback.
blocks.zh:
因为校正只取决于关键索引 我们的Triton内核直接加进去了
至在线软max环形圈内的每个积分瓦,保留
闪烁的注意 [21]. 我们避免蒙面负载 通过夹住离线键
索引和指定重复栏的偏差 - 10 9 - 10 {}。 这样可以避免粘贴和复制
K/V 变速器; 只有小偏差向量被加成 。 偏差也预估了
主机,避免内环内转换. 对于200200帧序列,我们
内核需要984 984 mss:只有4%的4QQ慢于无偏见的导火线注意,2.18×2.18\时速比倒数快.

blocks.en: A.2 Memory-Efficient K/V Matching
blocks.zh: A.2 内存有效 K/V 匹配

blocks.en:
Bipartite matching requires only the row-wise maximum similarity and argmax index, not
the full similarity matrix. Materializing the full matrix would require 27.25 27.25 GiB for a 200 200 -frame sequence. Even a chunked PyTorch [ 23 ] reference, which materializes 5,000 5{,}000 rows at a time, requires a 1.20 1.20 GiB temporary buffer. Our Triton kernel keeps
each score tile in registers and writes only the two required outputs, reducing this
temporary memory to 0.003 0.003 GiB.
blocks.zh:
Bipartite 匹配仅需要行形最大相似度和 argmax 指数, 不
完全相似的矩阵。 实现完整的矩阵需要27.25 27.25 GiB,200个框架序列。 甚至一个块形的PyTorch [23] 引用,一次实现5000 5{,}000行,都需要1.20 1.20 GiB临时缓冲器. 我们的三角内核
在登记册中每块计分,只写两个所需的输出,减少此值
临时内存为 0.003 0.003 GiB.

blocks.en:
The kernel trades a modest increase in runtime for substantially lower memory
use: the similarity kernel itself takes 482 482 ms against 330 330 ms for the
chunked reference at this shape. This overhead of roughly 150 150 ms
is small relative to the memory saved, since materializing similarity tiles
incurs a large transient VRAM cost and can become the limiting factor for long sequences.
blocks.zh:
内核交易运行时间稍有增加,以大幅降低内存
使用: 相似性内核本身需要482 482 ms,而330 330 ms用于
此形状的块引用 。 这笔费用大约150 150毫秒
相对于所保存的内存来说是小的,因为实现相似性牌
产生巨大的瞬态VRAM成本,并可能成为长序列的限制因素.

blocks.en:
The PyTorch reference delegates the 1,024 1{,}024 -dimensional dot-product reduction to its
matrix-multiplication backend. In our fused kernel, which additionally computes the
row-wise maximum and argmax, we partition the feature dimension into smaller tiles and
accumulate partial dot products.

矩阵乘法后端. 在我们的熔化内核中,它额外计算
按行最大和矩形,我们把特征尺寸分成小的瓦片和

blocks.en: Appendix D Merge-Operator Ablation

blocks.en:
The merge operator independently determines whether to merge queries with K/V tokens and
whether to correct each merged key’s logit by its token size.
Table S3 isolates these choices under an otherwise fixed
configuration. Merging queries forces all tokens within a group to share the same output,
whereas preserving queries retains within-group diversity but does not address the
attention-mass bias caused by K/V merging. The + log ⁡ s +\log s correction restores
the mass of the tokens each merged key represents and provides the larger accuracy gain. Together, query
preservation and the + log ⁡ s +\log s correction nearly recover no-merging accuracy, with the
benefit becoming larger at higher merge ratios.

blocks.en:
We choose the core blocks by measuring how much merging changes the
aggregator’s final representation. For each candidate set, we leave those blocks unmerged and apply merging
to every other block. We measure the relative Frobenius-norm deviation between the final
global-block outputs of the merged and unmerged models on the special tokens, and
normalize it by the deviation obtained when all blocks are merged. Because this
measurement uses no ground-truth annotations, the core blocks are selected without
reference to task labels.

我们选择核心块 通过衡量合并会改变多少
集合器的最后代表。 每一组候选人,我们让这些块不合并 并应用合并
到其他街区。 我们测量最终结果之间相对的弗罗贝尼乌斯-诺姆偏差
特殊标志上合并和未合并模型的全局块输出,以及
通过合并所有区块时获得的偏移来使其正常化. 因为这个
测量不使用地面真实说明,选择核心块时不使用
引用任务标签。

blocks.en:
We evaluate block sets rather than individual blocks. Simply ranking individual
blocks and selecting the top k k does not reliably find the best set. A
single-block measurement considers one block while all other blocks remain
unmerged, whereas the full model applies merging across multiple blocks. Merging
in one block can therefore change the token representations and
source–destination assignments used by later blocks.

blocks.en: Appendix G Comparison with AVGGT
blocks.zh: 附录G 与AVGGT的比较

blocks.en:
GPA-VGGT and AVGGT [ 3 ] share a two-stage structure: both replace early
global-attention blocks with frame attention and reduce the K/V set in later blocks
while preserving all queries. In the early stage, AVGGT restricts attention to
within-frame tokens, whereas GPA-VGGT augments each frame with a pooled shared
cross-frame K/V set. In the later stage, AVGGT retains K/V tokens at fixed spatial
strides, whereas GPA-VGGT selects them through bipartite merging. At an equal token
budget, AVGGT summarizes all removed tokens with a single unweighted mean K/V
pair, whereas GPA-VGGT aggregates each removed token into the retained token it most
closely matches and restores the corresponding attention mass through
the + log ⁡ s +\log s correction. The 128 128 -dimensional Gaussian projection reduces matching overhead,
enabling GPA-VGGT to retain fewer K/V tokens than AVGGT(2) while achieving both lower
runtime and higher accuracy.
